title: Embedding endpoint latency floor mitigation using adaptive shard coordinator and request shaping
creator: Ava Park
description: Goal: Reduce p99 and p999 tail latency on the embeddings/reranking endpoint without hurting overall throughput or fairness across tenants. Current production telemetry shows a stubborn latency floor driven by small, fragmented microbatches and shard hot-spots for multi-tenant workloads. This ticket implements an adaptive shard coordinator plus per-request shaping budget to smooth ingress, improve kernel selection accuracy, and preempt straggler-induced tail events.
background: Observed symptoms: 1) p99 for emb endpoint at ~720ms on large GPU nodes for common 512-dim models, 2) p999 spikes >1.6s during bursty ingress, 3) most tail cases correlate with sub-1KB requests that never accumulate into coalesced microbatches and cause kernel misprediction. Existing schedulers use static shard sizing and opportunistic coalescing which leaves small tail requests on slow execution paths. Related incidents: incident-2026-02-17 (embedding-regression) and telemetry dashboard 'emb-latency-prod-v2'.
approach: 1) Adaptive shard coordinator: dynamically adjust shard occupancy and group small requests into temporary shard windows based on short historical arrival rates and tenant weights. Coordinator will maintain per-shard token budgets and a eviction policy to avoid starvation. 2) Request shaping: attach a lightweight shaping token to each incoming request indicating max delay budget and preferred coalescing group; shaping is tenant-aware so high-SLA tenants can opt for shorter delay budgets. 3) Kernel hinting: use the coordinator's observed sequence-length histogram to send kernel hints to the runtime for more accurate kernel selection (fastpath vs generic). 4) Speculative prefill and warmup: for tenants with frequent small requests, pre-alloc KV cache and issue speculative prefill to amortize first-token cost. 5) Fallback policy: if shaping budget expires, route to a low-latency fastpath kernel with reduced batching but preserved correctness.

telemetry_goals: Reduce p99 from 720ms to <= 450ms and p999 from >1.6s to <=900ms for baseline 512-dim model under mixed tenants. Maintain throughput within +/-5% and no customers with >2x increase in median latency. Add new metrics: shard_fill_ratio, shaping_delay_ms, kernel_hint_match_rate.
acceptance_criteria: p99 and p999 targets met on production-like traffic during 48h A/B run
No regressions in throughput or 95th percentile for high-SLA tenants
Kernel hint match rate > 92% for requests with shaping_budget >=5ms
Runbook updated and rollback path validated
Code reviewed and security checklist passed
tests: Synthetic microburst harness that can replay tenant mixes and small-request-heavy traces
Chaos test: inject artificial slow kernels to validate fallback path
End-to-end integration test that asserts KV prefill correctness and no cache correctness regressions
Perf benchmark comparing static shard vs adaptive coordinator on staging GPU fleet
rollout_plan: Start with 5% of production traffic in us-west-2 (non-critical tenants) for 24h, monitor shard_fill_ratio, shaping_delay_ms, error rates, and latency SLOs. If metrics stable, step to 25% for 24h, then 50% for 48h. Maintain immediate rollback gate if p99 increases by >10% vs baseline or errors increase >0.5%. High-SLA tenants can be excluded from early rollout until validated.
operations_notes: Runbook located at https://confluence.internal/redwood/emb-shard-coordinator-runbook. Key run steps: disable coordinator via feature flag 'emb.shard_coordinator' to revert to static shards; clear shaping queues with admin tool 'ingress-rebalance'; to diagnose tails, capture shard_fill_ratio and per-shard latency histograms.
